description: Mercury is a chemical element with symbol Hg and atomic number 80, commonly known as quicksilver. It is a heavy, silvery d-block metal and the only metallic element that is liquid at standard temperature and pressure. It has the lowest freezing point, lowest boiling point, and narrowest liquid state range of any metal under standard conditions.
uses: Mercury is used in thermometers, barometers, manometers, sphygmomanometers, float valves, mercury switches, mercury relays, and fluorescent lamps, though its use has been reduced due to toxicity concerns. It remains in use in scientific research applications and in amalgam for dental restoration in some locales, and is still used in fluorescent lighting where electricity passed through mercury vapor produces ultraviolet light that causes phosphor to fluoresce.
characteristics: Mercury is a heavy, silvery-white metal that is liquid at standard conditions with a melting point of −38.83 °C and boiling point of 356.73 °C. Compared to other metals, it is a poor conductor of heat but a fair conductor of electricity, and was the first known superconductor discovered in 1911. Mercury readily dissolves many metals such as gold and silver to form amalgams, though iron is resistant to amalgam formation.
